basis: Part 121 applies to a facility required to register under section 415 of the FD&C Act (21 CFR 121.1). The registration rule exempts facilities regulated exclusively, throughout the entire facility, by USDA under the Federal Meat Inspection Act (21 CFR 1.226(g)). The shop handles only owner-delivered carcasses under the FMIA custom exemption and holds no FDA registration. Even a registered shop of this size would be a very small business (121.3), exempt except for documentation (121.5(a))

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
basis: No final rule. As proposed, food and agriculture entities are covered only above the SBA size standard, which is 1,000 employees for NAICS 311612 (13 CFR 121.201); the shop has no employees

obligation: USCG Cybersecurity in the Marine Transportation System rule
basis: Applicability is by MTSA facility, vessel or OCS facility status (33 CFR 101.605). The shop is a rural inland building on the owner's homestead with no MTSA security plan

obligation: FMIA custom exemption conditions (records, labels, ingredients, product protection, FSIS access)
basis: The shop prepares beef, pork, lamb and goat carcasses only for the owners of the animals and sells no meat, so it operates under the custom exemption in 9 CFR 303.1(a)(2). Its conditions are binding: sanitation standards (416.1-416.6, with listed exceptions), procedure and ingredient rules (318.5, 318.6, 424.21), "Not for Sale" marking (316.16, 317.16), custom records (303.1(b)(3)) plus Part 320 records, and FSIS access to records (300.6(b)(2), 320.4). FSIS reviewed the operation in March 2026
The registration rule exempts facilities regulated exclusively by USDA under the FMIA (21 CFR 1.226(g)). The whole shop operates under the FMIA custom exemption, and no wild game is accepted
417.2(a) applies to every official establishment. The shop is custom exempt, has no grant of inspection, and 417 is not among the conditions for custom operators in 303.1(a)(2) and (b)

obligation: FSIS 24-hour notice of adulterated or misbranded product in commerce
basis: Written for each official establishment; not among the custom exemption conditions. The shop's product goes back to the animals' owners marked "Not for Sale"
The duty falls on the person who registers a food facility (350f(a)); the shop registers none

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (data security, disposal and breach notice)
basis: "Covered entity" expressly includes a sole proprietorship (501.171(1)(b)). The custom records and booking submissions hold names with street addresses, phone numbers and emails of about 640 livestock and product owners, and no Social Security, driver license or financial account numbers. Whether a street address counts under the 2026 geolocation element (501.171(1)(g)1.a.(VII)) is an open question for counsel; until it is answered, the owner treats the records as personal information. The consumer reporting agency notice (501.171(5)) does not arise at about 640 individuals
No binding federal cybersecurity rule reaches the shop (see the rows above and below). The vertical profile names CSF 2.0 as the sector-neutral baseline, so the owner uses it as the benchmark

obligation: NIST Guide to Operational Technology Security
basis: The smokehouse controller and the cold-chain gateway are small connected devices on the shop Wi-Fi; SP 800-82 Rev. 3 informs the device rules in POL-01

obligation: Card processor merchant terms (card data protection and compromise reporting)
basis: The merchant terms require the shop to protect card data and report suspected compromise. Card data is encrypted at the processor's reader and no card numbers are stored on or pass through shop-managed systems. PCI DSS reaches the shop only through this contract

obligation: State AI laws on consequential decisions
basis: The chatbot makes no decision about a person (employment, credit, housing, insurance, education, health care, government or legal services)

obligation: FTC Act Section 5 (unfair or deceptive practices)
basis: Applies to the shop's own promises to customers; not decomposed into requirement rows

obligation: HIPAA Security, Privacy and Breach Notification Rules
basis: The shop is not a health care provider, health plan or clearinghouse (45 CFR 160.103) and holds no health information
The shop is a sole proprietorship, not a public company

obligation: FAR safeguarding and supply chain clauses
basis: The shop has no federal contracts or subcontracts
